Combine the quantitative and presence/absence tracks

Source: R/quant-stats.R
combine_quant_results.Rd

Merges test_differential() and test_detection() into one table per contrast and assigns each feature a Status: up/down when the moderated test passes both the FDR and the fold-change cut-off, exclusive_up/ exclusive_down when the feature is detected in min_detect units of one condition and in none of the other, ns otherwise.

Usage

combine_quant_results(
  diff_res,
  det_res,
  fdr = 0.05,
  log2fc = 1,
  min_detect = 2
)

Arguments

diff_res

Output of test_differential().

det_res

Output of test_detection().

fdr

Adjusted p-value cut-off for the quantitative test. Default 0.05.

log2fc

Absolute log2 fold-change cut-off. Default 1.

min_detect

Minimum number of units in which an exclusive feature must be detected in the condition where it is present (capped at that condition's number of units). Default 2.

Value

A data frame with the columns of both inputs plus Status (factor: up, down, exclusive_up, exclusive_down, ns).

Details

The exclusive flag is deliberately a detection-count rule, not a p-value cut-off: with the small designs typical of immunopeptidomics the Fisher exact test cannot reach a small p-value at all (a fully exclusive feature in a 3-vs-3 comparison gives p = 0.1, and no adjustment can improve on that), so gating the flag on the FDR would silently hide every on/off ligand. The Fisher p-values from test_detection() are carried along as supporting evidence and become decisive as the number of replicates grows.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
results <- combine_quant_results(res, det, fdr = 0.05, log2fc = 1)
table(results$Contrast, results$Status)
} # }
